alt: Schematic map of Europe's two camps: the Triple Alliance of Germany, Austria-Hungary and Italy (Dual Alliance 1879, Italy 1882) and the Triple Entente of Britain, France and Russia (Franco-Russian Alliance 1894, Entente Cordiale 1904, Anglo-Russian Entente 1907); the ententes were friendly understandings, not promises to fight.
caption: Figure: the alliance system before 1914 (schematic, not to scale)

alt: Timeline of the Anglo-Ndebele War from the Victoria incident of July 1893, through the battles of Shangani and Bembesi, to the entry into Bulawayo on 4 November 1893 and Lobengula's death in early 1894.
caption: Figure: timeline of the Anglo-Ndebele War, 1893-94

alt: Chart of Company government after the 1898 Order in Council: the British government's Royal Charter gave the BSAC power, the Resident Commissioner supervised it, and the Company governed through an Administrator, a Legislative Council and a Native Affairs Department with Native Commissioners.
caption: Figure: how the BSAC governed Southern Rhodesia after 1898

alt: Chart of the two Cold War blocs divided by the Iron Curtain: NATO (1949), SEATO (1954), Marshall Aid and West Germany against the Warsaw Pact (1955), Comecon (1949), the Cominform and East Germany.
caption: Figure: the western and eastern blocs and the Iron Curtain

alt: Bar chart of the 1980 common-roll election: ZANU-PF won 57 of the 80 seats, PF-ZAPU 20 and the UANC 3; the 20 white-roll seats all went to the Rhodesian Front.
caption: Figure: common-roll seats won in the February 1980 election (of 80)

alt: Timeline of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland: conferences from 1949, the Southern Rhodesian referendum of April 1953, Kariba Dam in 1955-59, emergencies in 1959 and dissolution on 31 December 1963.
caption: Figure: timeline of the Federation, 1949-1963

alt: Causes of the 1896-97 risings: long-term grievances (land, cattle, forced labour, hut tax, Native Police), the 1896 triggers (rinderpest, drought, locusts) and the opportunity created by the Jameson Raid, which led to the risings.
caption: Figure: grievances (grey), triggers (amber) and opportunity (green) behind the 1896-97 risings

alt: Timeline of the 1896-97 risings: the Jameson Raid, the Matabeleland rising in March 1896, the spread to Mashonaland in June, the Matopo indabas of August to October 1896 and the executions of April 1898.
caption: Figure: timeline of the First Chimurenga/Umvukela

alt: Timeline of the July Crisis of 1914: the Sarajevo assassination on 28 June, the blank cheque on 5-6 July, the ultimatum on 23 July, Austria-Hungary's declaration of war on 28 July, Russian mobilisation on 30 July and Britain's entry on 4 August.
caption: Figure: from Sarajevo to world war, 28 June-4 August 1914

alt: Chart of the League of Nations: the Assembly (all members) and the Council (permanent and elected members), with the Secretariat, Permanent Court of International Justice, International Labour Organisation and commissions below.
caption: Figure: organs of the League of Nations

alt: Timeline of Mao's China from the 1950 Agrarian Reform Law and the First Five-Year Plan of 1953 through the Hundred Flowers campaign, the Great Leap Forward of 1958 and the famine of 1959-1961 to the Cultural Revolution of 1966 and Mao's death in 1976.
caption: Figure: timeline of Mao's China, 1950-1976

alt: Schematic map: groups leaving the Zulu heartland after the Mfecane. Mzilikazi's Ndebele go via the Highveld to south-western Zimbabwe (c. 1838-1840), Zwangendaba crosses the Zambezi in 1835, Soshangane founds Gaza in southern Mozambique and Sebetwane's Kololo reach the upper Zambezi.
caption: Figure: main Mfecane migrations (schematic, not to scale)

alt: Six causes of the decline of the Mutapa state: succession disputes, Portuguese interference, breakaway provinces, the rise of the Rozvi, loss of trade income and Nguni invasions, all feeding into one outcome.
caption: Figure: causes of the decline of the Mutapa state

alt: Organisation chart of the Mutapa state: the Mwene Mutapa rules through a court and provincial chiefs over commoners and conquered peoples, orders go down, tribute and soldiers come up, and mhondoro spirit mediums advise the king.
caption: Figure: how the Mutapa state was organised (political structure)

alt: Chart of the nationalist parties: SRANC (1957, banned 1959), NDP (1960, banned 1961), ZAPU (1961, banned 1962), then ZANU (1963) and the People's Caretaker Council, both banned in August 1964.
caption: Figure: each nationalist party was banned and replaced, 1957-1964

alt: Chart of how the Nazi state controlled Germany after Hitler became Führer in 1934: terror and repression (SS, Gestapo, camps, courts), propaganda and culture (Goebbels, radio, press, rallies) and pressure on the churches.
caption: Figure: methods of Nazi control

alt: Chart of the Ndebele state: the king rules through izinduna and regiments living in regimental towns, Shona tributary communities pay tribute, and society has three groups, Zansi, Enhla and Hole.
caption: Figure: organisation of the Ndebele state

alt: Two lists side by side: the five organs of the OAU (Assembly, Council of Ministers, General Secretariat, Commission of Mediation, specialised commissions) and the seven organs of the African Union, which adds a Pan-African Parliament, Peace and Security Council, Court and civil-society council.
caption: Figure: organs of the OAU compared with the African Union

alt: Schematic map of the Pioneer Column of 1890: from Macloutsie in Bechuanaland past Fort Tuli, Fort Victoria and Fort Charter to Fort Salisbury, keeping to the east of Matabeleland and avoiding the Ndebele heartland.
caption: Figure: route of the Pioneer Column to Fort Salisbury (schematic, not to scale)

alt: Timeline from the Lancaster House Agreement of 21 December 1979 and the common-roll elections of 27-29 February 1980 to independence on 18 April 1980 and the renaming of Salisbury as Harare in 1982.
caption: Figure: timeline of the road to independence

alt: Timeline of the steps to the Second World War: Germany leaves the League in 1933, the Rhineland in 1936, the Anschluss in March 1938, Munich in September 1938, Prague in March 1939, the Nazi-Soviet Pact of 23 August and the invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939.
caption: Figure: timeline of the steps to war, 1933-1939

alt: Timeline from the Torwa state of about 1450, through Changamire Dombo's victories at Maungwe in 1684 and Dambarare in 1693, to the Nguni invasions of the 1830s and the Ndebele settlement of about 1838 to 1840.
caption: Figure: timeline of the Torwa and Rozvi states

alt: Timeline of Russia from 1915 to 1917: the Tsar takes command, Rasputin is murdered, the February (March) Revolution brings abdication, Lenin returns in April, and the Bolsheviks take power in the October (November) Revolution on 7 November 1917.
caption: Figure: timeline of Russia, 1915-1917

alt: Chart of SADC organs: the Summit of Heads of State and Government is the supreme body, with the Organ on Politics, Defence and Security, the Council of Ministers, the Secretariat in Gaborone and the SADC Tribunal, and National Committees in each member state.
caption: Figure: organs of SADC

alt: Timeline of the scramble for southern Africa from the Kimberley diamonds of 1867 and the Berlin Conference of 1884-85 to the British Ultimatum of 1890 and the Anglo-Portuguese Treaty of 1891.
caption: Figure: key events in the scramble for southern Africa, 1867-1891

alt: Timeline of the second phase of the armed struggle from the Altena Farm attack of 21 December 1972 and Mozambique's independence in 1975 to the Patriotic Front of 1976, the camp raids of 1976-78 and the Lancaster House conference of 1979.
caption: Figure: timeline of the second phase, 1972-1979

alt: Timeline of colonisation: Grobler Treaty (July 1887), Moffat Treaty (February 1888), Rudd Concession (30 October 1888), Royal Charter (29 October 1889) and the flag raised at Fort Salisbury on 12 September 1890.
caption: Figure: treaties, concession and occupation, 1887-1890

alt: Timeline from the Unilateral Declaration of Independence on 11 November 1965 through sanctions, the failed HMS Tiger and Fearless talks and the 1969 constitution to the 1970 republic and the Pearce Commission of 1972.
caption: Figure: timeline of UDI, 1965-1972

alt: Chart of the main organs of the United Nations: the General Assembly and the Security Council (five permanent members with a veto), with the Secretariat, International Court of Justice, Economic and Social Council and Trusteeship Council, and the specialised agencies WHO, UNICEF, UNESCO, FAO and ILO.
caption: Figure: main organs of the United Nations

alt: Timeline of Prussia's rise: Bismarck becomes Minister-President in 1862, Austria and Prussia defeat Denmark in 1864, Prussia wins at Königgrätz on 3 July 1866, the Treaty of Prague follows and the North German Confederation is formed in 1867.
caption: Figure: timeline of Prussia and Austria, 1861-1867

alt: Timeline from the Luxembourg crisis of 1867 and the Ems telegram of 13 July 1870 through France's declaration of war, the defeat at Sedan and the Republic of 4 September 1870 to the proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles on 18 January 1871.
caption: Figure: timeline of the war with France and the Empire, 1867-1871

alt: Five factors behind the First World War: the alliance system, the arms race, colonial rivalry, Balkan nationalism (long-term, grey) and the Sarajevo assassination of 28 June 1914 (trigger, amber), all leading to war in August 1914.
caption: Figure: long-term causes (grey) and the trigger (amber) of the First World War
